title: Unified adapter for embeddings + rerank: canonical error mapping and cursor semantics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: We have diverging behaviors between legacy embeddings+rerank endpoints and the new unified API surface. Differences include: (1) HTTP error code semantics (legacy clients expect 4xx/5xx shapes and specific code strings), (2) pagination semantics (cursor tokens vs page/limit style and whether cursors are stable across model variants), and (3) streaming/partial-result clients that rely on provisional rerank outputs. These differences are causing customer breakages when they upgrade SDKs or when we route requests to optimized model variants.
proposal: Deliver a compatibility adapter layer that sits in the API gateway for a deprecation window. Adapter responsibilities: (a) map our canonical error objects to legacy error codes and messages (maintain existing error_type and error_code strings), (b) translate pagination: accept legacy page/token params and synthesize canonical cursor tokens, and vice versa, ensuring cursor stability for the configured migration window, (c) support a streaming fallback mode that buffers and emits partial rerank streams in the legacy wire format so older stream consumers keep receiving incremental rank updates, and (d) emit verbose compat telemetry so we can monitor client usage and identify un-upgraded integrators.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Integration test suite (legacy client emulator) passes for: list embeddings + rerank flows, cursor advance/rewind, and simulated model-variant fallback.
2) Error mapping test matrix covers 12 common error classes and returns the legacy code+message shape.
3) Streaming legacy clients receive provisional rerank chunks within original timing SLAs for 95% of synthetic traces.
4) Metrics: compat-layer added latency P50 < 8ms, P99 < 35ms on typical traffic.
5) Migration playbook documented with rollback steps and communication templates.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy adapter behind feature flag for 5% of traffic to non-critical tenants (2 days). Phase 2 (ramped): 25% -> 50% over a week, monitor telemetry and error-surface. Phase 3 (opt-in window): expose opt-in toggle in Console for enterprise accounts to select adapter. Phase 4 (deprecate): announce 90-day deprecation after adoption reaches 95%.
migration_notes:
- For long-lived cursors, adapter will maintain a mapping table for 90 days to allow clients to rehydrate tokens.
- Encourage customers to migrate to canonical cursor token: provide SDK helper to translate and persist mapping.
- Documented changes to rate limits for paged rerank endpoints during compatibility mode.
risks:
1) State blow-up from maintaining mapping table for many cursors (mitigation: TTL and LRU eviction + metrics).
2) Behavioral drift for streaming: buffering could increase tail latency (mitigation: bounded buffer + backpressure signals).
3) Edge-case mismatch when model variant changes scoring semantics; may expose differing order for same cursor (mitigation: annotate compat tokens with model-version fingerprint).
observability_requirements: Emit the following labels on logs/metrics: compat_adapter=enabled, legacy_client=true/false, cursor_mapped=true/false, error_map=classname. Add a dashboard tracking: mapped_cursor_count, mapping_table_size, adapter_latency_p50/p95/p99, legacy_error_rate, and number_of_clients_using_adapter.
dependencies_notes: ENG-3921: Kernel-side changes to expose stable model-version fingerprint. PM-23845: earlier pagination playbook that informed cursor TTL and tooling.
qa_plan: 1) Build legacy-client emulator that uses historical request traces (sanitized). 2) Run compatibility harness across canary and staging. 3) Manual exploratory QA for streaming flows with boundary cursor cases. 4) Security review for any token translation/storage (keys rotated and no PII persisted).
